hook.kn: ಈ ತರಗತಿಯ ಪ್ರತಿ ವಿದ್ಯಾರ್ಥಿಗೆ ಒಂದೇ ಕ್ರಮ ಸಂಖ್ಯೆ, ಇಬ್ಬರಿಗೆ ಒಂದೇ ಸಂಖ್ಯೆ ಇಲ್ಲ. ಇದು ಏಕೈಕ ಫಲನ. ಎಲ್ಲ ಕ್ರಮ ಸಂಖ್ಯೆಗಳು ಬಳಕೆಯಾದರೆ ಅದು ಮೇಲ್ಮುಖವೂ ಹೌದು.

objectives.en: Prove a function is a bijection

narration.en: Every student in this room has exactly one roll number, and no two students share one. That is a one-one function. If every roll number is used, it is onto as well.
narration.kn: ಈ ತರಗತಿಯ ಪ್ರತಿ ವಿದ್ಯಾರ್ಥಿಗೆ ಒಂದೇ ಕ್ರಮ ಸಂಖ್ಯೆ, ಇಬ್ಬರಿಗೆ ಒಂದೇ ಸಂಖ್ಯೆ ಇಲ್ಲ. ಇದು ಏಕೈಕ ಫಲನ. ಎಲ್ಲ ಕ್ರಮ ಸಂಖ್ಯೆಗಳು ಬಳಕೆಯಾದರೆ ಅದು ಮೇಲ್ಮುಖವೂ ಹೌದು.

body.en: $f : X \to Y$ is one-one (injective) if $f(x_1) = f(x_2)$ implies $x_1 = x_2$. It is onto (surjective) if every $y \in Y$ is $f(x)$ for some $x \in X$, i.e. range = codomain. A function that is both is a bijection.
body.kn: f(x₁) = f(x₂) ⇒ x₁ = x₂ ಆದರೆ f ಏಕೈಕ (one-one). ಪ್ರತಿ y ∈ Y ಗೆ ಪೂರ್ವಪ್ರತಿಬಿಂಬ ಇದ್ದರೆ, ಅಂದರೆ ವ್ಯಾಪ್ತಿ = ಸಹಪ್ರದೇಶ ಆದರೆ f ಮೇಲ್ಮುಖ (onto). ಎರಡೂ ಆದರೆ ದ್ವಿಮುಖ (bijective).

narration.en: A function is one-one if different inputs always give different outputs. It is onto if every element of the codomain is actually reached. If it is both, it is a bijection.
narration.kn: f(x₁) = f(x₂) ⇒ x₁ = x₂ ಆದರೆ f ಏಕೈಕ (one-one). ಪ್ರತಿ y ∈ Y ಗೆ ಪೂರ್ವಪ್ರತಿಬಿಂಬ ಇದ್ದರೆ, ಅಂದರೆ ವ್ಯಾಪ್ತಿ = ಸಹಪ್ರದೇಶ ಆದರೆ f ಮೇಲ್ಮುಖ (onto). ಎರಡೂ ಆದರೆ ದ್ವಿಮುಖ (bijective).

body.en: If $n(A) = m$ and $n(B) = n$, there are $n^m$ functions from $A$ to $B$. When $m \le n$, the number of one-one functions is $n(n-1)\cdots(n-m+1)$. When $m = n$, a function between finite sets is one-one exactly when it is onto, and there are $n!$ bijections.
body.kn: n(A) = m, n(B) = n ಆದರೆ A ಯಿಂದ B ಗೆ nᵐ ಫಲನಗಳಿವೆ. m = n ಆದಾಗ ದ್ವಿಮುಖ ಫಲನಗಳ ಸಂಖ್ಯೆ n!.

narration.en: From a set of m elements to a set of n elements there are n to the power m functions. One-one functions number n P m, and when the sets have equal size there are n factorial bijections.
narration.kn: n(A) = m, n(B) = n ಆದರೆ A ಯಿಂದ B ಗೆ nᵐ ಫಲನಗಳಿವೆ. m = n ಆದಾಗ ದ್ವಿಮುಖ ಫಲನಗಳ ಸಂಖ್ಯೆ n!.

problem.en: Show that f : R → R, f(x) = 3x + 2 is a bijection.

steps.en: Onto: for any real y, take x = (y − 2)/3; then f(x) = y.
Both hold, so f is a bijection.

narration.en: Let us solve this together. Show that f : R → R, f(x) = 3x + 2 is a bijection.

problem.en: Is f : N → N, f(x) = x² one-one? Is it onto?

steps.en: In N, x₁² = x₂² gives x₁ = x₂ (no negatives), so f is one-one.
2 ∈ N, but no natural number has square 2.

narration.en: Let us solve this together. Is f : N → N, f(x) = x² one-one? Is it onto?

body.en: Sketch y = f(x). If some horizontal line cuts the graph twice, f is not one-one. If some horizontal line at a codomain value misses the graph, f is not onto.

narration.en: Horizontal line test. Sketch y = f(x). If some horizontal line cuts the graph twice, f is not one-one. If some horizontal line at a codomain value misses the graph, f is not onto.
Class quiz. Discuss, raise hands, and the monitor taps the class answer.

homework.en: Check whether f : R → R, f(x) = x³ is one-one and onto.

narration.en: Recap. One-one: f(x₁) = f(x₂) ⇒ x₁ = x₂. Onto: range equals codomain. Bijection = one-one and onto. Number of functions from m elements to n elements is nᵐ.
